minutes.headline: Commission approved several septic and other compliance certificates and two NOIs, and continued most hearings to October 21.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard a planning director presentation on four draft zoning amendments, then worked through a long hearing list. Most hearings were continued to October 21; the Sunny Hill Road driveway, the Goodrich Street irrigation pond and the Pleasant Street septic were approved. The commission also approved eight certificates of compliance and authorized spending on the Hollis Road house.

public_comment.topic: Archery deer season is open on conservation land; he recommended fluorescent clothing for hikers, especially near Duskon.
Member Andrea described the mushroom walk at the Lane property, with a large turnout. She raised dog waste and off-leash dogs on the trails and suggested signage or a future agenda item.
Abutter said the retaining wall at 386 Sunset Lane is dangerously deteriorated, with only a bungee-held gate, and that it could have been an emergency certification.
Abutter asked that no more trees be removed than necessary for the Goodrich Street irrigation pond.

budget_items.topic: Hollis Road house carpet and laundry room flooring
budget_items.what_was_said: Proposal with prevailing wage, tax-exempt status and W9, to be paid from the Hollis Road account, which holds enough to cover it.
The agent said the commission has full authority to use the account on other commission properties as well as the Hollis Road house.
A cap of $400 was proposed, then a cap of $700 was moved and approved, including supplies.
An electrician is preparing an estimate, with donated materials, and added code-compliant closet light fixtures at a small per-item cost.

decisions.decision: Plan to bring a custodian/caretaker for the Hollis Road house onto the town payroll through a town meeting article, then seek applicants.
Volunteers will start painting at Hollis Road on Saturday. Non-commission helpers must sign waivers, which the agent will print.

For 3 Wilderwood the commission asked for 3:1 replacement of the two maples, a wall across the beach at a lower height, a replacement planting plan and schedule, and a revised drawing. The pines are to stay.
For 37 Fire Road 10 the commission asked to remove the sandy beach area and to try to keep the tree.
Possible placards on dog waste and leash rules at Lane and Largetown Forest entrances were discussed, and a future agenda item was suggested.

what_happened.line: The commission approved three notices of intent: a driveway crossing at Sunny Hill Road, an irrigation pond on Goodrich Street, and a septic replacement on Pleasant Street.
Most other hearings were continued to October 21, including 3 Wilderwood Avenue, 37 Fire Road 10, 386 Sunset Lane, 143 Island Road, 404 Page Street, and the Mass Ave sites.
The commission approved certificates of compliance for properties on Sunset Lane, Island Road, Laurel Lane, Beiel Street and White Street, each by 5-0.
For the Hollis Road house, the commission approved a flooring proposal paid from the Hollis Road account and capped paint and supplies spending.
The planning director presented four draft zoning amendments, with comments due at the end of November.

why_it_matters: Approved notices of intent set the conditions for work near wetlands in town, and the continued hearings on Wilderwood, Fire Road and Sunset Lane stay open to public comment on October 21.
The draft zoning amendments on senior housing, inclusionary, cluster and minor site plan rules could change what can be built in town, and residents can still comment before the end of November.
Hollis Road house repairs are drawing on a dedicated commission account, and a plan to put a caretaker on the town payroll would need a town meeting article that residents would vote on.
watch_next: October 21: continued hearings resume, including 3 Wilderwood Avenue, 37 Fire Road 10 and 386 Sunset Lane.
End of November: deadline for comments on the four draft zoning amendments.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on most continuances and certificates of compliance, and the Hollis Road flooring approval matches at $9,411.50. They differ on several votes: 108 Sunny Hill Road, 404 Page Street, 3 Wilderwood, the paint spend, the Snow Riders motion, and how the 171 Island Road and 68 Laurel Lane certificates were voted. A reader should check the 108 Sunny Hill Road item first, since ours records an approval and the official minutes record a continuance with no stated result.
